About Us

DriveWealth is on a mission to make investing easier. We believe that everyone should have the ability to control their financial future, and that access to financial markets should not be limited by geography, wealth, or legacy systems. We are a global B2B financial technology organization dedicated to democratizing access to financial independence around the world. Our mission is realized through an API-based platform, empowering our partners to offer seamless investing and trading experiences to clients worldwide, all from their mobile devices. Our technology provides partners with a modern, extensible toolkit, enabling traditional investment workflows and innovative techniques like fractional share ownership. DriveWealth has evolved into a global platform offering trading of US equities, mutual funds, ETFs, fixed income, and options.

There’s never been a better time to build a category-defining business and there has rarely been a team better positioned for this opportunity. Our culture blends the pace and agility of a fintech start-up with the impact, stability, and discipline of Wall Street. We encourage creativity and experimentation while ensuring institutional-grade execution and regulatory compliance in everything we do. Join us and help build the future of global investing!

About The Role

This is the first product role DriveWealth has placed in-market, and you will own what it becomes. You are the product voice for our partners in India across the full platform: equities, mutual funds, ETFs, fixed income, and options, plus the account opening and money movement capabilities underneath them. Partners in this market bring requirements that are specific, sometimes ambiguous, and always urgent, and your job is to convert them into scoped, sequenced, shipped work. You will not run a dedicated engineering team. Your leverage comes from judgment, credibility, and your ability to pull the right product owners and engineering leads across the platform onto the right problem. You own the call on which requests become roadmap, which get an alternative solution, and which get a clear no. You will work in close partnership with our regional Head of Sales, and you will represent this function directly to partners and to product leadership. Success in year one looks like partners in India who feel heard, a delivery record they can point to, and a repeatable model we can stand up in the next jurisdiction.

What You’ll Do

Become the primary product point of contact for our partners in India, and build the relationships that surface real requirements before they become escalations
Translate partner asks across all asset classes, accounts, and money movement into requirements, user stories, and documentation that other product owners and engineering teams can execute against without a translation layer
Sequence and track delivery across multiple product domains, holding the through-line from request to launch when no single team owns the whole thing
Partner with the regional Head of Sales on commercial context, partner priorities, and competitive pressure in-market
Test every request against platform capability and local jurisdictional requirements, and propose the alternative when the answer is no
Spot the patterns across requests that point to a platform gap, and drive them into the appropriate domain roadmap yourself
Decide when to push back, when to escalate, and when to absorb complexity to keep delivery moving, without needing that judgment checked
Speak for this function in partner, sales, and product leadership forums on status, tradeoffs, and constraints
Write the playbook for in-market product delivery, with an eye to what should scale to the next jurisdiction

You Bring

Minimum 7 years of experience in Financial Services and/or Fintech or equivalent industries, in product management, business analysis, or a senior partner-facing technical role
Bachelor's Degree in computer science, engineering, finance, or equivalent in relevant experience
Experience with trading platforms, brokerage, or fintech infrastructure
Experience analyzing data using SQL and relevant BI tools
FINRA Securities Industry Essentials (SIE) completion, or a commitment to acquire within the first year with support from your Manager
A track record of ownership and disciplined execution in high-stakes environments
The ability to prioritize ruthlessly, focussing on what’s critical versus important to drive work to completion
A client-oriented mindset with an understanding of how your work impacts partners
Strength in cross-functional partnership with the judgment to coordinate across multiple teams
A bias toward transparency, accountability, and responsiveness in everything you do
You’re committed to continuous improvement and implicitly believe that we > I. 
Impeccable high integrity, sound judgment, and a deep respect for risk, control, and operational excellence

Location

This role is open to candidates in the following locations: Hyderabad, IN - On-site

This role is expected to come into the office on a cadence set by the Hiring Manager/Team.
If you're not based in one of the location listed above, this role is not a fit, and we cannot accommodate remote work outside this location.

Working at DriveWealth

We do our best work when we're in the same room. To maintain the speed our partners expect, our New York, Chicago, and Lithuania teams work in office on a hybrid schedule. We've found that being physically side-by-side is the only way to solve complex problems in real-time and stay truly accountable to the products we ship. When you're here, you're working directly with the people making the decisions.

To support that work, we provide competitive compensation, equity, and a 401(k) match. We also offer Medical insurance, Dental insurance, Vision insurance, Disability insurance, and Paid Parental Leave, along with a wellness reimbursement, a company-provided phone, and a personal development allowance. Finally, we value the time you spend away from the office with generous Paid Time Off (PTO) and observed holidays.

Work Authorization

Applicants must possess the legal right to work in the country where the position is located at the time of application. DriveWealth requires all employees to provide original documentation verifying their work authorization on or before their first day of employment.

For US-based roles: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without the need for current or future visa sponsorship. DriveWealth does not provide visa sponsorship or support for employment authorization, including transfers, at this time. Offers of employment are strictly contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the Company.

How We Think About AI

We leverage AI to work smarter and move faster. We seek AI-curious talent who are proactive about using emerging tools to increase signal quality, reduce friction, and improve outcomes to deliver products faster, provide better service to our partners, and to streamline processes. Your ability to leverage our internal tools and technology to drive results is as important to us as your core domain expertise.

Compensation

Pay is generally based on the level, complexity, responsibility, location, and job duties/requirements of the specific position. We then source candidates with the requisite skills, expertise, education, training, and experience. If you are selected for an interview, please feel welcome to speak to a recruiter about our compensation philosophy and other available benefits. This role is eligible for base, bonus, equity, 401(k) match, and heavily subsidized benefits and perks.

Job Title: Executive Product Owner - Enterprise Knowledge Fabric

Location: Bangalore

Business & Team:

The Enterprise Knowledge Domain is a newly established capability and a foundational pillar of the Group's artificial intelligence strategy. The team will define how organisational knowledge is structured, governed, connected and made available across the enterprise. It will work closely with engineering, architecture, data, scientific and business communities to create trusted knowledge foundations that support enterprise search, knowledge discovery and intelligent systems.

Within the domain, the Knowledge Fabric team builds and operates the federated context layer that connects these foundations to people and AI agents, and the Product Owner makes sure it is adopted and delivers value.

Botsync builds and deploys autonomous mobile robot systems for material movement in factories and warehouses across multiple geographies, for enterprise customers including Caterpillar, Ford, Nestlé and Coca-Cola. Our AMRs operate in live industrial environments where reliable autonomous navigation, localization, docking, coordination and charging must work — continuously and predictably.

Our product stack spans AMR hardware and onboard software that run on the robot, through to SyncOS, the software layer that orchestrates fleets, connects equipment, and integrates with enterprise systems. This gives our teams the chance to solve customer operational problems end-to-end: from motion and sensing on the robot, to fleet-level coordination, to the operational visibility and intelligence we bring to every deployment.
The Opportunity

We are looking for a senior robotics product leader who's passionate about pushing what a physical system can reliably do — and building the discipline to prove it before it ever reaches a customer site.

You will own hard product problems end to end: deciding which performance and operating limits are worth pushing, setting the bar a robot must clear before deployment, and turning every field failure into a sharper answer next time.

You will lead and grow the product team shaping our robotics platform — setting product direction and ensuring decisions across hardware, firmware and robot software add up to one coherent product.

The Role
Expand the AMR operating envelope - Own the AMR product roadmap across hardware, firmware and robot software. Decide which performance and operating limits are worth pushing, set and defend targets across mobility, navigation, docking, material handling and fleet reliability, and quantify the engineering and vendor trade-offs behind each investment
Prove reliability before deployment - Own how we establish confidence that a robot will perform under real operating conditions before it reaches a customer site. Turn recurring failures into permanent verification scenarios, and continuously raise the evidence bar a product or release must clear before deployment
Learn from the fleet - Turn field performance into systematic product learning. Build the mechanisms to recognize known failure patterns from telemetry, errors and logs, automatically assemble the evidence engineers need to investigate them, and close the loop from field failure to root cause to product improvement to verification
Lead the robotics product function - Lead and grow the PM team responsible for the robotics product. Translate customer needs, fleet evidence and technology opportunities into a prioritized roadmap; distinguish one-off customer requirements from reusable product investments; establish measurable outcomes and acceptance criteria; and partner across engineering and ops teams to deliver outcomes

What are we looking for:
Essential-
8–10 years across robotics, industrial automation or autonomous systems, combining hands-on engineering depth with real product ownership
Has owned reliability, validation, deployment risk or field performance across multiple customer deployments
Technically credible enough to challenge engineering and vendor trade-offs on their own terms: sensors, motion control, power systems, navigation-stack behaviour and system integration
Comfortable refining a gated hardware development process — sharpening what each gate requires, tightening go/kill criteria, as the product and organization mature
Able to specify what must be measured, then hold a release to that measurement when the ship date is under pressure
Strong product judgement on what should become reusable platform capability versus what should remain bespoke
Leads through influence: aligns engineering, deployment and customer teams, and other product managers, without owning them on an org chart

Highly Desirable-
End-to-end system exposure spanning mechanical, electrical and software domains
Experience operating across multiple customer geographies where site conditions and operating assumptions differ materially
Exposure to AMR safety and functional-safety standards, and familiarity with what simulation and pre-deployment test infrastructure can't prove about physical systems before deployment
Have working knowledge of ROS 1/ROS 2, and of the telemetry, logging and bag data a fleet emits
Direct experience with AMR, AGV or autonomous-vehicle fleets in manufacturing, warehousing or intralogistics

Product Manager — Post-Order Experience

Department: Product Location: Mumbai, Onsite Experience: 3–4+ years

About The Role

Purplle is hiring a Product Manager to own the post-order experience — everything a customer

goes through after placing an order: order tracking, cancellations, returns and refunds, and customer

support. This is the part of the journey that decides whether a customer trusts us enough to come

back.

You'll own these flows end-to-end, treat them as products to be improved rather than systems to be

maintained, and be accountable for the metrics that show they're working — reachability of support,

resolution quality, and a smooth experience even when things go wrong.

What You'll Do

Own the post-order journey end-to-end — order tracking, cancellations, returns and refunds,

and order care — and set the roadmap, balancing quick wins (e.g., real-time tracking updates)

with longer-term bets (e.g., predictive self-service).

Make customer support reachable and effective: improve discoverability of help across key

journeys, strengthen self-service and automation, and ensure clean escalation to a human

agent when needed.

Reduce avoidable contacts (WISMO, status checks) by fixing root-cause friction in tracking and

communication — without making support harder to reach.

Raise resolution quality, measured by repeat contacts, reopens, and post-resolution satisfaction

— not just the volume of cases closed.

Monitor behavioural analytics regularly, spot abnormal changes, and turn insights into a

prioritised set of product fixes.

Partner across Engineering, Design, Customer Support Operations, Logistics, and Finance to

ship improvements and align on SLAs, policies, and delivery realities.

What We're Looking For

3–4+ years in a product role, ideally in e-commerce, marketplaces, or consumer tech.
Experience owning customer-facing journeys or post-order / order-management / customer-

support flows.

Hands-on with data — comfortable with SQL and analytics tools (e.g., Mixpanel, Looker,

Tableau) to frame hypotheses, run experiments, and measure impact.

A systems thinker who maps complex end-to-end flows and finds the highest-leverage fixes.
Customer-obsessed, with strong written communication and the ability to influence cross-

functional teams without authority.

Nice to Have

Exposure to support tooling (Zendesk, Gladly, or similar), conversational automation / chatbots,

and returns or logistics platforms.

Familiarity with India's e-commerce dynamics — COD, regional cohorts, and delivery realities.

About Purplle

Purplle is one of India's leading beauty e-commerce platforms, with 30M+ users and one of the most

diverse beauty catalogs in the country. We're building the operating system for beauty — connecting

consumers, brands, and beauty professionals in one ecosystem. This role owns the moment of truth:

what happens after the order, where customer trust is won or kept.

About Company

Founded in 2011, Purplle has emerged as one of India’s premier omnichannel beauty destinations, redefining the way millions shop for beauty. With 1,000+ brands, 60,000+ products, and over 7 million monthly active users, Purplle has built a powerhouse platform that seamlessly blends online and offline experiences.

Expanding its footprint in 2022, Purplle introduced 6,000+ offline touchpoints and launched 100+ stores, strengthening its presence beyond digital. Beyond hosting third-party brands, Purplle has successfully scaled its own D2C powerhouses—FACES CANADA, Good Vibes, Carmesi, Purplle, and NY Bae—offering trend-driven, high-quality beauty essentials.

What sets Purplle apart is its technology driven hyper-personalized shopping experience. By curating detailed user personas, enabling virtual makeup trials, and delivering tailored product recommendations based on personality, search intent, and purchase behavior, Purplle ensures a unique, customer-first approach.

In 2022, Purplle achieved unicorn status, becoming India’s 102nd unicorn, backed by an esteemed group of investors including ADIA, Kedaara, Premji Invest, Sequoia Capital India, JSW Ventures, Goldman Sachs, Verlinvest, Blume Ventures, and Paramark Ventures.

With a 3,000+ strong team and an unstoppable vision, Purplle is set to lead the charge in India’s booming beauty landscape, revolutionizing the way the nation experiences beauty.

At FirstClub, we are building a new kind of quick commerce from the ground up, and the supply chain is where that promise is won or lost. The Supply Chain Product team builds the systems that decide what we buy, where it sits, how it moves and what we promise each member. Every order that reaches a member on time, fresh and complete is the output of our products.


The team's charter spans the full supply chain:


- Buying & Sourcing: demand-led purchase planning, vendor management, PO lifecycle and inbound scheduling.


- Collection Centers: first-mile intake, quality checks, grading and consolidation of fresh and farm produce.


- Distribution Centers (DCs): inbound, putaway, storage, picking, packing, outbound and returns.


- Middle Mile: DC-to-Club House replenishment, trip planning, vehicle utilization and inventory movement.


- Club Houses: receiving, storage, pick-pack, cycle counts, freshness and wastage control.


- Inventory Management: single source of truth for stock, ageing and expiry, replenishment and inventory accuracy across nodes.


- Capacity Management: labor, slot, storage and throughput planning across nodes and time of day.


- Promise Engine: what we promise each member availability and delivery ETA based on live inventory and capacity.


Why FirstClub


- Build, don't babysit: Much of our supply chain stack is being built right now. You will design core systems, not just tune someone else's.


- Small team, big surface area: You'll own outcomes that would sit with a whole team at a larger company.


- Fast loops: Ship on Monday, watch it run on a Club House floor by Wednesday, improve it by Friday.


- Ground truth over slide decks: Our PMs spend real time in DCs, Collection Centers and Club Houses, not just in dashboards.


- Scrappy beats perfect: We'd rather run a pilot this week than polish a plan for next quarter.


- Your fingerprints on the company: The decisions you make now shape how FirstClub scales to every new city.


The role


As a Senior Product Manager, you will own the end-to-end supply chain product charter at FirstClub from how we source and buy, through Collection Centers, DCs and the middle mile, to inventory in our Club Houses and the promise we make each member. Your mandate is to build a high-control, intelligent and scalable supply chain that improves availability, freshness and speed while driving down cost per order and wastage.


This isn't a role where you inherit a mature platform and keep it running. You'll build core pieces of FirstClub's supply chain while the business grows around them: making calls with incomplete data, getting your hands dirty on the floor, and setting how product works across the charter. You'll shape how inventory moves across the network, how frontline teams work, and how FirstClub scales to new cities without losing control or quality.


What you will do


- Own the product vision, strategy and roadmap across Buying & Sourcing, Collection Centers, DCs, Middle Mile, Club Houses, Inventory Management, Capacity Management and the Promise Engine.


- Set and own the north-star metrics for the charter: availability and fill rate, promise adherence (promised vs. actual), inventory accuracy, days of inventory, wastage and shrinkage, cost per order and throughput per node.


- Partner deeply with Supply Chain, Category, Operations and Finance leadership to find the biggest ground-level problems and convert them into a prioritised, outcome-driven roadmap.


- Architect the core systems with Engineering: a single source of truth for inventory across nodes, a demand-led buying and replenishment engine, and a Promise Engine that balances availability, capacity and speed in real time.


- Build capacity planning across labour, slots, storage and vehicles, so the network flexes for peaks, new categories and new cities.

POSITION PURPOSE:

The Principal Product Manager is responsible for the overall product vision, strategy and roadmap across a specific Platform or domain and works on the hardest problems within the Platform. They make specific contributions to Product and Platform delivery by working directly with Product Squads within the Platform to ensure each product is oriented toward business outcomes that improve company performance. The Principal Product Manager partners directly with the Platform Lead and their teams to deliver. The Principal Product Manager is an expert communicator that represents the Platform by presenting to senior leaders across Bayer and externally to accelerate digital transformation and build Bayer’s reputation as a digital leading company.

Principal Product Managers apply the product management discipline to some of the hardest problems within the Platform. They ensure that products are fulfilling their primary purpose to enable users to perform tasks that create value for the company by:

-Setting strategic vision for the product to ensure the customer and their needs are at the center; and ensuring team priorities are supporting business outcomes for customer, product, technical and enabling teams. This requires continual alignment of the product strategy and objectives with customer, product, technical, and enabling teams

-Managing the product backlog, which prioritizes the work of the assigned squads, to achieve the vision and aligned strategy.

To successfully manage these areas of responsibility, Principal Product Managers must have a deep understanding of the product domain, related technology, and architecture.

YOUR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Product Management

The product manager is accountable for the overall success of a product throughout its lifecycle, from conception to decommissioning. They identify domain needs, develop, and validate product concepts, and build a business case. They oversee the product's build and launch, including any sourced services; as well as ensure product availability, stability, and compliance needs are met. Product managers collaborate with various teams, including product development, marketing, finance, legal, manufacturing, operations, and sales, as needed, to ensure cohesive progress and success.

Product Managers drive agile best practices with the team to improve delivery, including continuous planning ahead of each development cycle (e.g. sprint planning) and working together to co-create user stories aligned with the product backlog prioritization. In addition to guiding the team product managers have duties like market opportunity identification, competitive analysis, sales enablement, or monitoring domain performance.

Stakeholder Engagement

It is vital for the product manager to identify their key stakeholder group. Though many strong and loud opinions will be expressed, an effective product manager uses discretion to deliver their product in a way that meets the needs of users and stakeholders who will ensure value is realized for Bayer. Stakeholders should trust that the product manager not only understands their needs but will actively work to ensure their needs are met while delivering the product.

Product Strategy

The product manager must provide strategic leadership with full end-to-end ownership for their assigned products throughout the entire product lifecycle. They are responsible for planning and optimizing capabilities to deliver business outcomes in the most efficient way. Product managers require strong strategic planning, decision making, and influencing skills to balance the needs of users and various stakeholders.

Product Discovery & Delivery

The product manager is responsible for creating comprehensive product roadmaps, to clarify user needs and non-functional requirements. They provide product oversight by tracking and reporting progress against 90-day outcomes and overall product health (including budget responsibilities). They also plan and manage product delivery while streamlining the corresponding backlog. Product managers are responsible for monitoring user feedback and metrics to co-create solutions that drive a better user experience and deliver more business value. They leverage Design Thinking methodology starting with user needs to prioritize problems and through discovery they perform usability, feasibility, business fit and value testing to determine the optimal solution.

People & Collaboration

Product managers must proactively communicate and collaborate with product users and stakeholders, which requires strong strategic communication skills. Effective cross-functional collaboration is critical for product managers, bringing together diverse skills and knowledge to deliver a valuable product. It's important to maintain strong and productive working relationships with colleagues in product management, engineering, and other technically focused organizations. The Principal Product Manager serves as a Product Management Chapter Lead for their Platform, where they are responsible for development of the product management community to improve product management and agile practices, fostering a culture of excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.

10 or more years of experience as a product manager

Job Description:

About Nubra: Nubra is a trading platform for people who take trading seriously, whether they scalp index options on expiry day or run multi-leg strategies over weeks. We've built Smart Flexi Orders, multi-strike charts, tick-level option chain data, a multi-leg strategy builder, smart watchlists, automation APIs, and flexible collateral management, and we're still early in what we want the product to become.

Most of our users have tried other platforms before us. They know exactly what breaks at 9:15 AM, which order types are missing, and how many taps it takes to adjust a position when the market moves against them. Our job is to make those moments better. You can see the product at nubra.io.

The role: You'll own the roadmap for the parts of Nubra that traders use every single session: order placement and execution, the option chain, the strategy builder, charts, and our automation APIs. You'll work day to day with engineering and design, and closely with compliance and risk, since almost everything we ship has a regulatory angle. This is a hands-on role. You'll write the specs, sit in on technical discussions about latency and data feeds, look at the numbers yourself, and talk to traders every week.

Coming from e-commerce or D2C? We'd like to hear from you. Some of the best product thinking for a trading app comes from people who have built checkout flows, high-volume order systems, or products where a few seconds of delay costs real money. What we need from you is a genuine interest in markets and the willingness to get fluent in options and derivatives quickly. If you already trade on the side, even better.

What you'll be responsible for:

Roadmap and product direction:
Own the roadmap for order types, option chain, strategy builder, charts and automation APIs.
Decide what we build next and, just as often, what we don't. Be able to explain the reasoning to the team.
Keep a close eye on other trading and investing platforms in India and abroad, and know where we're ahead and where we're behind.
Building and shipping:
Turn trader workflows into clear specs that engineers can build from without a dozen follow-up calls.
Work with engineering on the trade-offs that matter in trading: speed, reliability, and accuracy of data under heavy market load.
Work with design so that complex features (multi-leg orders, margin, Greeks) feel simple to use.
Plan releases carefully. A bug in an order flow is not the same as a bug in a settings page.
Users and data:
Speak with active traders regularly through calls, support tickets, community channels and usage data.
Define what success looks like for each feature and track adoption, retention, order success rates and trading behaviour.
Run experiments where it makes sense and be honest about results when something doesn't work.
Compliance and risk:
Work with compliance and risk teams so that new features meet SEBI and exchange requirements from day one, not as an afterthought.
Understand how margin, collateral and risk checks affect the user experience, and design around them sensibly.


Your first six months, roughly:

Month 1: Use the product the way our users do, with real trades if you're comfortable. Read support tickets, sit with engineering, and get to know the order lifecycle end to end.
Months 2 to 3: Take ownership of one feature area and ship your first meaningful improvement. Set up the metrics you'll use to judge it.
Months 4 to 6: Own the roadmap for your area, with a clear view of priorities for the next two quarters and the user evidence to back them.


What we're looking for:

3 to 6 years of product management experience in trading, broking, fintech, capital markets, e-commerce or D2C.
You've shipped consumer products end to end, ideally ones with high transaction volumes, real-time flows or demanding power users.
You're comfortable with data. You can write or read a query, build a funnel, and tell the difference between a real trend and noise.
You understand trading concepts such as order types, options, derivatives and market data, or you're clearly on your way there.
You write clearly and can get engineering, design, compliance and business teams to agree on a plan.
You're interested in markets. Not as a line on your CV, but because you actually find them interesting.


Good to have:

Personal trading experience, especially in F&O.
Prior work at a broker, exchange or prop trading firm.
Experience with options or derivatives platforms specifically.
Working knowledge of SEBI regulations and NSE/BSE rules.
A background in analytics or quant, or experience with real-time data systems.
Experience building payments, checkout or other high-trust flows where conversion and reliability both matter.


How we work: We start with the user. Here that means thinking like a trader. If you can't explain why a trader would care, it probably doesn't belong on the roadmap. We move quickly. Markets change fast and so do our users' expectations. We'd rather ship, learn and fix than wait for a perfect version.

We use data, and we make calls. Numbers inform our decisions, but we don't hide behind them. Sometimes you have to back your judgement. We own outcomes. Shipping a feature isn't the finish line. Whether it helped traders is what counts.

What you get:

Ownership of the core of a trading product used by active traders every market day.
Problems that are genuinely hard: real-time data, complex instruments, regulation and user experience all in one place.
A small, capable team where your work is visible and your opinion counts.
A steep learning curve in capital markets, if you're new to the space.
Competitive pay with performance-based incentives.

We are seeking an experienced, high-caliber Vice President – Fixed Income Product Owner to take end-to-end ownership of the Fixed Income (FI) Book of Work. In this critical leadership role, you will define and execute the strategic product roadmap across Post-Trade Processing, specifically focusing on Fixed Income Settlement, Confirmation, and Regulatory Reporting.

As a VP Product Owner, you will serve as the strategic bridge between Front Office, Market Operations, Market Controller, and Global Technology Delivery teams. You will manage competing priorities, negotiate complex requirements, and interface regularly with senior leadership to ensure timely and high-impact delivery of strategic initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Product Strategy & Book of Work Ownership
Take full end-to-end accountability for defining, prioritizing, and delivering the Fixed Income Post-Trade Book of Work.
Formulate a multi-year product roadmap aligned with organizational goals, regulatory imperatives, and operational efficiency targets.
Translate complex business problems into clear product epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and measurable business outcomes.
Manage capacity and budget allocations across development pods, optimize resource utilization and release velocity.
Domain Leadership: Post-Trade Processing & Regulatory Compliance
Settlements: Drive transformation across global settlement mechanisms (e.g., Euroclear, Clearstream, DTC, Fedwire, local market CSDs), fail management, and cash/securities reconciliation.
Trade Confirmation & Matching: Lead product enhancements for electronic trade affirmation/confirmation platforms (e.g., Trax, DTCC CTM, SWIFT messaging: MT/MX ISO 20022).
Regulatory Reporting: Oversee product compliance with international regulatory reporting regimes impacting Fixed Income (e.g., MiFIR/MiFID II, EMIR, Dodd-Frank, FINRA TRACE, CAT, CSDR).
Proactively monitor market structure changes, industry mandates, and central clearing counterparty (CCP) rules to ensure product adaptability.
Senior Stakeholder Management & Negotiation
Build and sustain relationships with key stakeholders, including Desk Heads, Operations Leadership, Technology Directors, Risk & Control Partners, and Legal/Compliance Officers.
Navigate competing priorities across multiple business lines through structured trade-off analyses, data-driven insights, and executive negotiation.
Run steering committees, backlog prioritization sessions, and executive status reviews, clearly communicating product vision, risks, and ROI.
Agile Delivery & Execution Excellence
Act as the dedicated Agile Product Owner across cross-functional engineering and QA squads.
Lead backlog grooming, sprint planning, sprint reviews, and acceptance sign-offs.
Define and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and key risk indicators (KRIs) to quantify product adoption, operational STP (Straight-Through Processing) rates, and risk mitigation.
Champion best-in-class product management practices, ensuring adherence to change governance, SDLC frameworks, and audit controls.

Qualifications & Candidate Profile

Experience & Domain Knowledge

Education: Bachelor’s degree in finance, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (Master’s or MBA preferred).
Experience: 8+ years of total financial services / fintech experience, with at least 4+ years in a senior Product Owner, Product Manager, or Business Analyst role.
Subject Matter Expertise: In-depth knowledge of Fixed Income asset classes (Bonds, Treasuries, Repos, Security Lending and Borrowing instruments) and post-trade lifecycle.
Core Technical/Operations Acumen:
Solid grounding in SWIFT messaging standards (ISO 15022 and ISO 20022), FIX protocol, and trade flow architecture.
Comprehensive understanding of bilateral and central clearing, tri-party repo mechanics, and exception handling workflows.
Practical experience delivering regulatory reporting solutions for post-trade transaction reporting.

Leadership & Soft Skills

Stakeholder Negotiation: Proven ability to influence and align senior stakeholders with divergent agendas.
Analytical & Problem-Solving Skills: Adept at dissecting complex workflow bottlenecks and formulating scalable, automated solutions.
Agile Leadership: Strong familiarity with Scrum/Kanban frameworks, JIRA/Confluence, and modern product management tools.

Communication: Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills suited for C-suite and executive audiences.

jobs.sourceTitle: Director, Product Management — Core Database Engine & AI
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Our Company

At Teradata, we believe that people thrive when empowered with better information. Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform activates enterprise intelligence by unifying data, knowledge and business context to achieve tangible outcomes. With Teradata, organizations can provide agents with full context for impact when it matters. Our solution lets businesses connect and scale on premises, in the cloud, or through a hybrid approach. Teradata delivers real business value with AI. 

What You'll Do

In this role, you will lead product strategy and execution for Teradata's core database engine: the massively parallel query engine behind every workload on the platform. You will shape the roadmap across the optimizer, execution runtime, workload management, and Global Planner, and own how the engine performs on native storage, cloud object storage, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake. 

This role sits at the intersection of the database engine and AI. AI agents are becoming the dominant consumers of enterprise data, issuing high volumes of exploratory, speculative queries, while GenAI and machine learning can improve the engine from the inside. Every core component needs to be rethought in this light, and you will lead that rethink and turn it into a roadmap engineering can build. 

Two things anchor the role. Performance: you will spend significant time inside real workloads, query plans, and benchmarks, working with engineering to deliver measurable gains release after release. SQL: you will be the steward of Teradata SQL, the surface customers live in, making its syntax, semantics, and ergonomics simpler, more expressive, and safer for developers, analysts, and AI agents. 

Strategy: Own the engine vision and multi-year roadmap, co-owning architecture direction with senior engineering leaders and making principled trade-offs across performance, cost, and complexity. 
AI and agents: Lead the rethink of every core engine component for AI agents as the new dominant workload, and apply GenAI and ML inside the engine to make it faster and more autonomous. 
Optimizer, execution, and workload management: Agents send many redundant queries. Explore optimizing across queries, sharing intermediate results, and returning early or approximate answers. Apply learned cardinality and cost models and LLM-assisted rewrite, with guardrails that protect plan stability. Define how workload management absorbs bursty machine traffic through agent identity, priorities, and budgets. 
Performance: Work hands-on with engineering on query plans, regressions, and bottlenecks. Own the benchmark suite and KPIs (latency, concurrency, plan stability, price-performance), including agentic workloads, and build regression gates into releases. 
Open Table formats: Own the engine side of Iceberg and Delta Lake (scan planning, pruning, pushdown, write paths) so customers never trade performance for openness. Automate statistics, clustering, and compaction with AI. 
SQL language and query interface: Design features that turn complex problems into simple, readable queries, reduce footguns while keeping power and backward compatibility, and stay aligned with ANSI SQL. Make the dialect something agents can safely generate and execute, and let agents steer with cost estimates, plan explanations, and hints. 

Who You'll Work With

You will work with senior database engineering leaders, performance engineering, AI platform teams, the open table format product team, sales engineering, and executive leadership across the US, Europe, and India. This role starts as an individual contributor, leading through technical depth and influence and mentoring Staff-level PMs. It may grow into managing a team of product managers. 

What Makes You a Qualified Candidate

15+ years in databases, query engines, or distributed data systems, including senior product management or equivalent principal or staff engineering experience 
Expert understanding of database internals: query planning, cost-based optimization, execution models, and MPP trade-offs 
Deep SQL expertise: a heavy SQL user (data engineer, analyst, or DBA) with strong opinions on language design, ergonomics, and compatibility 
A hands-on performance mindset: reading query plans, designing benchmarks, and finding root causes with senior engineers 
A strong working understanding of LLMs and AI agents, and an informed view on how they change database design and how ML can improve database internals 
Architecture-level knowledge of Snowflake, Databricks, and ClickHouse, and fluency in lakehouse architecture and open table formats 
Degree in Computer Science or a related field; an MS or PhD in databases, distributed systems, or ML for systems is a plus 

What You'll Bring

First-principles thinking and good taste: willingness to question long-standing database assumptions, a preference for elegance over verbosity, customer obsession, daily use of GenAI tools, and the credibility to earn the trust of senior engineers 
The ability to read research critically, separate promise from hype, and design experiments to prove value, with a track record of setting multi-year platform strategy 
A plus: experience designing SQL features or language extensions, hands-on work with optimizers or learned database components, open-source contributions, or publications at SIGMOD, VLDB, or CIDR

We prioritize a people-first culture because we know our people are at the very heart of our success. We embrace a flexible work model because we trust our people to make decisions about how, when, and where they work. We focus on well-being because we care about our people and their ability to thrive both personally and professionally. Position Overview

The Experienced Product Owner is an experienced, functionally deep Workday professional who owns one or more Workday modules end-to-end on behalf of Revantage and its PortCos. This is not a passive coordination role — it is an active, hands-on domain mastery role. You are the subject-matter expert, the decision-maker, the stakeholder champion, and the product strategist for your assigned module(s). You will work across a complex multi-PortCo environment, running user forums, managing the release roadmap, driving adoption, and continuously finding ways to extract more value from the platform. This role focuses on the US Payroll & Benefits Module. Additional module expertise is a plus.

Key Responsibilities

Domain Ownership & Functional Mastery

Own your assigned Workday module(s): US Payroll & Benefits end-to-end — from strategy and design through configuration, testing, deployment, and ongoing optimization.
Develop and maintain deep functional expertise in your domain(s), staying current with Workday product updates, roadmap changes, and community best practices.
Serve as the primary point of contact and escalation resource for your module area across all PortCos.
Maintain comprehensive knowledge of how your module(s) interact with upstream and downstream systems and processes — and design solutions with those dependencies in mind.
Think beyond Workday: identify complementary or supplementary technologies that could enhance capability in your domain — whether that is AI-powered tools, third-party integrations, or adjacent platforms.

PortCo Engagement & Stakeholder Management

Build and maintain strong relationships with HR leaders, operations teams, and business stakeholders across multiple PortCos.
Act as a trusted advisor — understanding each PortCo's unique workforce model, business context, and HR priorities.
Run structured Product Owner forums, working groups, and user communities to surface requirements, share updates, and drive alignment.
Manage competing priorities across PortCos with transparency — communicating trade-offs, timelines, and decisions clearly to all stakeholders.
Facilitate requirements workshops and design sessions, translating business needs into clear, actionable Workday solutions.

Roadmap & Release Ownership

Own and maintain the product roadmap for your module(s) — balancing strategic enhancements, PortCo-driven requirements, bug fixes, and Workday release adoption.
Evaluate every Workday bi-annual release for impact and opportunity within your domain — leading opt-in decisions, testing, and rollout planning.
Prioritize the backlog in collaboration with stakeholders, the Functional Architect, and People Technology leadership.
Ensure all enhancements are delivered with appropriate change management, training, and communications to end users and HR teams.
Track and report on the delivery and benefit realization of roadmap initiatives.

Hands-On Delivery

Remain hands-on with Workday configuration in your module area — able to configure, test, validate and deploy. 
Lead user acceptance testing (UAT) for enhancements and releases within your domain.
Create design documents, configuration specifications, and test plans before deployment.
Own day-to-day delivery.

Ecosystem & Innovation Thinking

Continuously evaluate the HR technology landscape for innovations relevant to your module area — e.g., AI in recruiting, manager effectiveness tools, payroll analytics.
Propose and build the business case for technology enhancements or new tool adoption where Workday alone does not fully meet business needs.
Collaborate with vendors (Workday, Paradox, HiredScore, Peakon, etc.) to stay ahead of product developments and advocate for Revantage's priorities.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of Workday functional experience with deep, hands-on expertise in at least two Workday modules.
Demonstrated experience owning a Workday module in a production environment — including enhancements, releases, stakeholder management, and roadmap ownership.
Nice to have experience working in a multi-entity, multi-PortCo, or shared-services HR technology model.
Strong understanding of Workday business process configuration, security roles, reporting, and calculated fields.
Proven ability to engage and influence senior HR stakeholders without direct authority.
Experience running forums, steering committees, or user communities across a distributed stakeholder base.
Global Workday implementation or support experience — able to navigate multi-jurisdiction complexity.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills — able to translate technical concepts for business audiences and vice versa.

Module-specific Experience

US Payroll

Payroll processing, tax configuration, and compliance — configuration and operational support.

Payroll Processing: Pay group setup, payroll calendars, run categories, gross-to-net calculation, and on/off-cycle run management.
Earnings & Deductions: Earning codes, deduction codes, arrears handling, garnishments, and pay component mapping from time and compensation.
Tax Configuration: Federal, state, and local tax setup, reciprocity rules, tax withholding elections, and year-end W-2 processing.
Compliance: ACA reporting, FLSA overtime, pay equity audits, and regulatory filing support.
Integrations & Reporting: GL mapping, bank file generation, payroll reconciliation, and audit-ready payroll registers.

US Benefits

Benefit plan configuration, open enrollment, and compliance — configuration and operational support.

Plan Configuration: Medical, dental, vision, FSA/HSA, life, disability, and voluntary benefit plan setup including carrier connections.
Eligibility & Enrollment: Eligibility rules, dependent coverage, qualifying life events, passive and active enrollment configuration.
Open Enrollment: OE event setup, employee self-service configuration, enrollment windows, and communication triggers.
ACA Compliance: 1095-C configuration, measurement periods, affordability calculations, and IRS filing support.
Integrations & Reporting: Benefit carrier file feeds, COBRA administration handoffs, benefit cost reporting, and enrollment audits. 

Preferred Qualifications

Workday Pro certification in one or more relevant modules.
Experience with third-party HR technology integrations and vendor management.
Exposure to change management methodologies and communication planning.
Prior experience in private equity, financial services, or multi-company real estate environments.
Familiarity with Agile or product management frameworks (backlog management, sprint planning, road mapping tools).

Revantage is a Blackstone portfolio company and a leading provider of corporate services across Blackstone's Real Estate portfolio. Headquartered in Chicago, Revantage supports a diverse and complex ecosystem of portfolio companies (PortCos) spanning residential, commercial, logistics, hospitality, and life-sciences real estate globally — across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.

Our People Technology team sits at the centre of this multi-entity, multi-jurisdictional operating model. We run a single Workday tenant that serves a federated landscape of PortCos, each with its own workforce, HR policies, compensation structures, payroll requirements, and compliance obligations. Responsibilities

Defining measurable success criteria for each initiative and tracking outcomes such as usage, conversion, willingness to pay, and support requirements. 
Making evidence-based go/no-go recommendations, transferring validated products to established product teams with a documented roadmap and operational runbook, and recording lessons from unsuccessful experiments. 
Providing weekly updates to the Chief Product Officer on progress, risks, ownership, and deadlines. 
Selecting the most effective technical approach for each concept, evaluating whether to build, buy, reuse, or adopt open-source solutions.

Ensuring MVPs are sufficiently production-ready for real customer environments, including packaging, safe deployment, rollback procedures, and observability. 
Collaborating with architecture and product teams to ensure successful MVPs can be integrated without requiring extensive redevelopment. 
Leading and developing a small, distributed engineering team through regular one-to-ones, goal setting, performance reviews, and career development. 
Managing recruitment activities, including defining role requirements, conducting technical interviews, onboarding, and mentoring engineers. 
Establishing effective remote working practices that support asynchronous collaboration, documented decisions, transparent communication, and regular product demonstrations. 
Promoting AI-augmented engineering practices by coaching the team on effective coding-agent use, including prompt quality, context management, code review, iteration, and error recovery. 
Using AI coding agents to accelerate prototyping, generate test datasets, and prepare customer-facing materials.

At least 5 years of professional software engineering experience.

About Techdome

At Techdome, we turn AI ambition into enterprise-grade products. Our engineers, designers, and AI specialists build LLM-powered applications, RAG systems, conversational assistants, autonomous agents, and workflow automation for clients in FinTech, Healthcare, E-commerce, EdTech, Logistics, and SaaS. Every product ships with the integrations, security, and compliance that enterprise clients demand.

Why This Role Exists

Anyone can get a GenAI prototype working in a weekend. The hard part is everything after: passing a security review, staying inside budget, keeping costs per query sane, and earning the trust of real users.

We’re looking for a Product Manager who treats that hard part as the real job. You’ll own products end to end, from the first client conversation through launch and long-term growth, and you’ll be the person who spots the vague requirement, the missed handoff, or the quiet risk while it’s still cheap to fix.

What You’ll Own

Product vision and scope

Shape a client’s idea into a clear product definition with realistic milestones, timelines, and budgets.
Go deep on each client’s industry, regulations, and compliance obligations, and convert them into requirements engineers can build from without guessing.

Taking GenAI from prototype to production

Partner with ML engineers to harden LLM, RAG, agent, and automation prototypes into reliable, scalable, and safe systems.
Define the metrics that matter in production, including accuracy, latency, evaluation scores, and cost per query, and review them continuously.
Make sure every AI feature integrates cleanly with client systems via APIs and meets enterprise expectations for security, data privacy, and uptime.

Leading across disciplines

Align UI/UX, frontend, backend, mobile, QA, DevOps, and business analysts so handoffs are explicit and nothing relies on assumption.
Plan team capacity and keep every party accountable to their commitments.
Manage third-party partners, including LLM and cloud providers.

Managing risk, change, and communication

Run structured change control whenever scope, timeline, or budget shifts.
Surface and escalate delivery, technical, and AI-specific risks early: hallucinations, prompt injection, data leakage, bias, and runaway costs.
Track work in JIRA or Azure DevOps and give clients and leadership clear, no-surprise updates.
Use AI tools to accelerate documentation, planning, tracking, and reporting.

What You Bring

Must have

2+ years as a Product Manager shipping complex enterprise software on time and on budget.
Hands-on GenAI experience, ideally having launched at least one LLM, RAG, or agent-based product, plus a solid grasp of the AI lifecycle and its risks.
A track record of leading cross-functional teams across design, engineering, QA, and DevOps.
Working knowledge of Agile (Scrum/Kanban) and Waterfall, and of tools like JIRA, Azure DevOps, Trello, or Asana.
Enough technical depth in the SDLC, APIs, microservices, databases, cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), and CI/CD to challenge estimates and earn engineers’ respect.
Sound judgment on risk, change, vendors, and stakeholders.
Clear, confident written and verbal communication, including with senior client executives.

Nice to have

Familiarity with LLM evaluation, guardrails, and cost-optimization practices.
PMP, PRINCE2, CSM, CSPO, or an AI/cloud certification.
Deep domain expertise in FinTech or Healthcare.
Experience across industries and the curiosity to pick up a new one fast.

How We’ll Measure Success

Day 30: You know how Techdome delivers, you’ve met the team, and you’re up to speed on active client projects.
Day 60: You independently lead at least one project, owning the plan, the risks, and the client relationship.
Day 90: You land a key milestone, make a visible improvement to how we run projects, and have earned the trust of both team and clients.

What’s In It For You

Technically demanding GenAI work across multiple industries.
Daily collaboration with seasoned designers, engineers, QA specialists, and AI experts.
A genuine say in how projects are planned, run, and delivered.
Room to build deep expertise at the frontier of GenAI.

Own feature prioritisation and release decisions with Engineering and UI/UX, and be able to state the cost and the benefit of each choice. A roadmap that only says yes is a backlog.
Identify and evaluate AI, Generative AI and automation opportunities, and assess each on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value before it reaches the roadmap.
Define product success metrics before the work starts, instrument the product to measure them, and read the results honestly afterwards.
Contribute to product positioning, pricing, go-to-market strategy and commercial viability, working with Sales and Marketing.
Build shared context across the organisation so that teams can make decisions without routing every question through you.
Work closely with the Founder, Engineering, UI/UX, Sales and other stakeholders to align on product direction and drive execution.

What You Will Not Own
Product Manager and Project Manager are used interchangeably across the market. At 2Base, they are different roles, so the boundary is stated rather than assumed.
Client project delivery. Project Managers own client engagements, schedules, and escalations.
Engineering architecture and implementation. You own what and why; Engineering owns how. Where the two conflict, you negotiate rather than instruct.
UI/UX design execution. The design function designs. You own the user outcome and brief, review and decide against it.
Final product investment and budget approval. The Founder decides what the product is funded to do and over what horizon. You own the case that decision is taken on.
Client-specific commercial negotiations. Pricing and packaging of the product itself is yours; client contracts are not.

Requirements
Experience

6–12 years in the technology industry, with at least 4 years in Product Management or direct product ownership.
At least one product you took from concept or early development to actual customer usage, with a clear view of what happened after release. A product you inherited fully formed and maintained is a weaker signal than a smaller one you shaped.
A decision not to build something, and what it cost you to hold that line.
Direct work with engineering teams through a build, not across a handover, with enough understanding of software development, technical feasibility, APIs, integrations and cloud applications to judge what a decision will cost.
AI and Emerging Technology
Practical exposure to AI-powered products, Generative AI, machine learning or automation-driven solutions.
The ability to tell a capability apart from a product, and to assess an AI use case on feasibility, scalability, cost and business value rather than on novelty.
Product Judgement

You can describe how you decided what to build: the evidence you had, the evidence you wanted and did not have, and what you did about the gap.
You can reason about a product commercially. Who pays, what for, and what has to be true for the numbers to work.
You can hold a position with a founder, an engineering lead or a client, and change it when the argument against you is the better one. Knowing which situation you are in is the skill.
You write and present clearly. Most of a product manager's influence here travels as writing, and a requirement that is ambiguous on Monday becomes an argument three weeks later.
Ways of Working
You start by asking rather than deciding. The first months are spent understanding users, the business model, what has already been attempted, and how decisions are actually made here.
You work independently and establish your own processes. There is no research function and no analyst to brief.
You influence without formal authority. Nobody in this structure reports to you, and the roadmap holds because people agree with it.
You can make a decision that leaves someone unhappy, explain the reasoning, and keep working with them. Trade-offs are the job, and somebody loses every time one is made.
Education

A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

What We Are Not Looking For
Stated now rather than at the end of a multi-stage process.
Project or delivery managers looking to change title. The skills overlap less than the market suggests, and this is not a promotion path from delivery.
Business analysts who have written specifications against requirements someone else set. Valuable work; different work.
Candidates whose account of a product is the features it shipped, with no view on whether it should have shipped them.
Anyone who needs an established research function, design system and process in place before they can start.

Benefits
A growth-driven environment with opportunities to lead, innovate, and upskill continuously.

About the Role

DexCare is building the AI-first patient navigation platform that health systems rely on to connect patients with the right care, fast. Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with Security, Engineering, Compliance, and Commercial teams to ensure the platform meets healthcare-grade security and privacy requirements (HIPAA, SOC 2, FedRAMP) without slowing down product velocity.

Roadmap & Prioritization: Translate platform reliability, security, and scalability needs into a prioritized backlog; make explicit build-vs-buy and sequencing tradeoffs.




What You'll Bring

7-9 years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion of that in platform, infrastructure, or identity/access domains.

Direct experience with authentication/authorization systems, multi-tenant SaaS architecture, or API platform products.

Comfort operating at a technical level — you can read an API spec, participate in architecture discussions, and push back credibly with engineering.

A track record of balancing security/compliance requirements against usability and delivery speed.

Strong written and verbal communication; able to translate technical tradeoffs for both engineering and executive audiences.

Has migrated a legacy system to multi-tenant SaaS with live customers

Experience in healthcare technology, regulated industries, or enterprise B2B SaaS is a strong plus.




Why This Role Matters
Identity and access aren't a back-office concern at DexCare — they're the foundation that makes every other product trustworthy and scalable. As DexCare grows its health system footprint, the decisions you make about tenancy, entitlements, and access control directly shape how fast the company can bring new customers and capabilities online.

jobs.sourceTitle: Senior Hardware Product Manager - IoT Wireless
jobs.descriptionHtmlOrText:
Silicon Labs (NASDAQ: SLAB) is the leading innovator in low-power wireless connectivity, building embedded technology that connects devices and improves lives. Merging cutting-edge technology into the world’s most highly integrated SoCs, Silicon Labs provides device makers the solutions, support, and ecosystems needed to create advanced edge connectivity applications. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, Silicon Labs has operations in over 16 countries and is the trusted partner for innovative solutions in the smart home, industrial IoT, and smart cities markets. Learn more at www.silabs.com.
Meet the Team
IoT is the only focus area for Silicon Labs and is one of the most visible and fastest growing segments of the semiconductor industry. Our portfolio of industry leading wireless solutions includes Bluetooth, Zigbee, Thread, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, Wi-Sun, Proprietary Wireless and other emerging technologies driving the next generation of IoT smart connected products. With the addition of AI acceleration, rich MCU content combined with best-in-class software stacks, tools and development environments we offer compulsive and complete solutions to customers.

As a member of the Hardware Product Management team, you will be responsible for the Silicon Labs IoT products starting from concept to plan and customer alphas. You will be required to interact with a wide range of cross functional teams including silicon design, product test, validation, software product management & engineering, project management and business management to ensure the best of the products come to the market.

As a team, hardware product management:

Provides leadership and vision on IC product roadmap and requirements.
Continuously improves our portfolio offering, balancing business needs with R&D efficiency.
Creates product roadmaps based on various segment inputs to meet the requirements for a diverse range of applications

This is one of the few functions where you will have the great opportunity to discuss with top executives regarding strategy and execution on a day-to-day basis, thus having invaluable amount of learning. 

Come and join us in our goal to become the undisputed leader in wireless connectivity for IoT! 

Responsibilities
Define SoC product requirements, features, specifications, and system KPIs for core CPU, co-processors, accelerators, power management, digital and analog peripherals, security sub-system, radio sub-system, and packages.
Map market systems application requirements to product use cases, including system block diagrams, compute and peripheral requirements, and protocol stack features and performance requirements for Wi-Fi, Matter, Thread, ZigBee, Bluetooth Low Energy, Bluetooth Classic, Sidewalk, Wi-SUN, and proprietary protocols.
Define hardware and evaluation tools for customers, including debug interfaces such as JTAG, SWD, ETM trace, PTI, virtual communication port requirements, and user interfaces such as push buttons, LCDs, LEDs, analog joysticks, and RHT sensors.
Collaborate with leaders and individual contributors across functional teams such as IC design, product test, software development, product and segment marketing, applications, operations, and sales to develop long-term innovation ideas, roadmap, and silicon definition.
Drive the product development process from concept through definition and pitch the most promising product ideas to executive staff.
Conduct key competitive analysis, including tear-down at the die level and various spec analyses, to provide conclusive takeaways for design, specification, and fighting guides.
Manage the entire portfolio of scalable products with clear mapping to target applications. 

Skills You Will Need
Minimum Qualifications
BSEE/BSCS (or equivalent) and 6+ years of experience in semiconductor product management or IoT industry
Core development experience in IC front end / architecture / verification / embedded systems
Knowledge of key architectural considerations for PPA, including power estimation, die size estimation, and fundamental process node technology principles.
Knowledge of Wireless Modem and RF Design principles for any of Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, 802.15.4, and other Low Power Wireless standards
Proven ability to work successfully at a technical level with cross-functional engineering teams, including hardware and software engineers 
Experience developing business cases for Technology investments working with Business Unit partners, sensitivity analysis of business case to variables under consideration. 
Excellent communication and presentation skills, especially to executive management

The following qualifications will be considered a plus:
Development experience in either wireless or wired communication protocols
MBA or equivalent business graduation

Benefits & Perks
Not only will you be joining a highly skilled and tight-knit team where every engineer makes a significant impact on the product; we also strive for good work/life balance and to make our environment welcoming and fun.

Overview

Join the Intuit Platform and Development Xcceleration group as a Senior Staff Product Manager. The PDX group builds the foundational capabilities that developers across Intuit rely on to build and run flagship applications on cloud native infrastructure at scale. Intuit believes in open source, both as a consumer and a contributor, and our engineers participate actively in communities including CNCF, Istio, and Argo.

We're looking for a product leader who can own two connected platform domains: the systems that provision and run Intuit's cloud infrastructure, and the systems that make Intuit's APIs and services usable by AI agents, not just human developers. You'll set direction for how infrastructure gets provisioned against policy, and for how AI agents discover, integrate with, and operate Intuit's internal services with less and less human intervention over time.

This role carries senior staff scope. You'll set product strategy independently, make tradeoffs other teams will build against, and represent these platforms directly to engineering and executive stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Own the product strategy and roadmap for Intuit's infrastructure orchestration and provisioning platform, working closely with the engineering teams who build and operate it.
Own the product strategy and roadmap for Intuit's agent-readiness platform, which evaluates how usable Intuit's internal APIs and services are for AI agents and drives the work that closes the gaps.
Define the metrics that matter for each platform, from infrastructure reliability and provisioning speed to how much manual work it still takes before an agent can operate a given capability end to end, and use those metrics to prioritize the roadmap.
Partner with the teams that define platform policy, identity, access, lifecycle rules, so that what you build upholds that policy rather than duplicating or drifting from it.
Work with capability teams across Intuit to help them raise their agent-readiness scores, generate the integration assets they're missing, and turn what used to be manual, tribal-knowledge work into something an agent or a new engineer can follow directly.
Represent both platforms to engineering leadership and cross-functional stakeholders, with a clear narrative tying platform investment to developer productivity and to Intuit's broader AI strategy.
Build and run a scrum team based in India, setting the cadence, backlog discipline, and quality bar that let a distributed team ship independently.

Qualifications

10 or more years of product management experience, including platform, infrastructure, or developer-tools products.
Direct experience with AI-enabled products or platforms, with a strong enough technical foundation to work through integration and architecture tradeoffs with engineering.
Strong experience with AI Evals, model evaluations, technical use cases, shared platform capabilities, driving adoption and growth of platform capabilities, and leveraging AI to assess technical capabilities, and agentic PDLC.
A track record of owning a product end to end: setting strategy, defining success metrics, and driving a roadmap that a distributed engineering team executes against.
Comfort partnering across adjacent platform teams where ownership boundaries matter, and judgment about when to defer to another team's policy versus when to push back.
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical tradeoffs to both engineers and executives.
Experience managing or closely partnering with engineering teams based in India strongly preferred.
Undergraduate degree in computer science or a related technical discipline required. Equivalent professional experience will be considered. Advanced degree or MBA preferred.

Intuit provides a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. This position may be eligible for a cash bonus, equity rewards and benefits, in accordance with our applicable plans and programs (see more about our compensation and benefits at Intuit. Pay offered is based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and work location. To drive ongoing fair pay for employees, Intuit conducts regular comparisons across categories of ethnicity and gender.

About The Team & Value Stream

Broad enough to translate framework capabilities into partner value, drive Solutions Exchange as a product led growth surface, and build the business case for API monetization. You'll move between architecture discussions with engineers, roadmap reviews with senior leadership, and go to market conversations with the Global Alliances team, sometimes all in the same week.

We're looking for someone who has genuinely internalized this shift, someone who reaches for an AI agent before a spreadsheet, who accelerates their PM work with agentic tools, and who understands how integration infrastructure must evolve to serve agentic consumers, not just human triggered workflows.

Lead data import/export and encryption strategy. Drive the Workflow and Integration Bryte AI Frontdoor. Own the AI powered interface for integration creation and workflow setup, from a partner or admin describing what they want in natural language to a configured, validated integration running in production.

Define integration standards and developer experience. Drive integration standards across domain teams to reduce time to market for new partner integrations through reusable components and configuration driven development. Own the developer portal, API reference materials, and SDK guidance.

Work as an AI native PM and raise the bar for those around you. Use AI agents daily across PRD drafting, technical research, document synthesis, metrics analysis, and stakeholder communications. Communicate strategy and roadmap to senior leadership and partners. Translate integration platform investments into business outcomes for engineering and product leadership. Represent the integration platform story externally to key partner organizations and internally to Global Alliances.

About You

We're looking for a builder. Someone who understands that integration infrastructure is not plumbing, it is product. Someone who has shipped developer facing platforms, has the technical credibility to shape architecture decisions, and has the commercial instincts to drive ecosystem growth and monetization. This role requires both worlds: you need to earn the trust of principal engineers in a webhook architecture discussion and then turn around and build the partner GTM case for the same capability.

What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.

At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.

Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality.

If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. Glean is seeking a Product Manager to help solve a ubiquitous problem that all knowledge workers in the world struggle with on a daily basis. Principal Product Manager, ASPM

Qualys is looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead ASPM (Application Security Posture Management), within the Enterprise TruRisk Management platform. ASPM provides unified visibility, risk-based prioritization, and integrated remediation to help organizations manage application security risk continuously and autonomously. As the PM, you will define the roadmap and execution strategy for how customers discover, consume, prioritize, and remediate application security risk, while driving ideas to increase product adoption and grow the ASPM business.

This is a high-impact role at the intersection of Application Security, vulnerability management, and Agentic AI. You will work closely with Engineering and Design to turn ideas into scalable, customer-facing capabilities; validate them with customers; partner with Marketing on go-to-market execution; and work with Sales to drive adoption and business growth.

What You’ll Own

Define the roadmap, execution plan and success metrics for ASPM. 
Build capabilities that help customers discover, prioritize, and remediate application security risk based on discovery, exploitability, application criticality, and business impact.
Partner with Engineering and Design and Threat teams to build the intelligence foundation for ASPM, including data ingestion, normalization, correlation, enrichment, scoring, and AI-assisted experiences.
Engage AppSec leaders, vulnerability managers, DevOps practitioners to uncover customer problems, validate solutions, and shape the ASPM roadmap.
Shape how ASPM intelligence powers ETM, TruRisk, risk operations, and Agentic AI-driven decision-making.
Partner with GTM teams on launches, enablement, positioning, and competitive differentiation. 


What Success Looks Like

ASPM becomes the application risk intelligence layer for ETM customers.
Customers cut through application security noise and focus on the exposures that matter most.
Qualys research and threat intelligence are transformed into scalable, actionable application security insights.
ASPM drives adoption, expansion, and differentiation for ETM.
AI and automation accelerate analyst productivity and decision-making without introducing black-box risk.


Required Experience

Minimum 8 years of product management experience, including 5+ years in cybersecurity or enterprise SaaS. 
Experienced in one or more of the following domains: ASPM, API security, Web App Security (SAST, DAST, and SCA), Vulnerability Management
Ability to work deeply with engineering, threat research, design, and security teams. 
Strong product judgment, customer discovery skills, and ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear customer value. 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for executive, customer, analyst, and internal audiences. 
Ability to learn quickly and keep up with fast changing AppSec domain
Familiarity with CVE, CVSS, EPSS, CISA KEV, MITRE ATT&CK, and related security frameworks. 


Preferred Experience

Some knowledge of Agentic AI and AI security would be highly preferred
Prior hands-on experience as Application Security Analyst or Pen-tester is a big plus


Why This Role Matters

ASPM is a critical part of Qualys’ vision for Enterprise TruRisk Management. It brings together application findings, vulnerability management, Qualys research, asset context, and business risk to help customers move from reactive application security to proactive, risk-based Application Security Posture Management.

This role will help shape how Application Security, Vulnerability Management, AI, and automation come together to power the next generation of Application Security Posture Management.
